text:
Priya (CS): 2026-03-15 16:08 UTC — Customer 'acme-app' opened support ticket: intermittent 502/504 from hosted inference in eu-1, started ~16:00, observed ~8% failure rate for a handful of endpoints. They included a repro and example client logs.
Alex (SRE): Oncall here, starting triage. Priya can you paste the sample request and request-id?
Priya (CS): Request ID r-abc123, endpoint /v1/generate, model=redwood-large. Sample curl they used: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"hello"}'
```
Priya (CS): They say retries usually succeed after 2-3s; failure started after a config push around 15:58 UTC.
Alex (SRE): I'm pulling gateway and auth-proxy traces now. Initial glance shows auth token refresh p95 spiking and auth-proxy returning 504s to gateway.
Miguel (Eng): Looking at auth-proxy logs from eu-1: I see a burst of KMS 429s and then timeouts. Sample lines: 
```
[2026-03-15T15:59:58Z] auth-proxy: fetch_token start (tenant=acme-app)
[2026-03-15T15:59:58Z] KMS -> 429 TooManyRequests
[2026-03-15T16:00:02Z] auth-proxy: timeout waiting for KMS -> returning 504 upstream
[2026-03-15T16:00:03Z] gateway: upstream auth-proxy 504 -> client 502
```
Sara (PM): How many customers impacted? CS mentioned acme-app + 2 others. Need comms if broader.
Nora (Oncall): Mitigation options: (A) enable short-lived local token caching on auth-proxy to avoid synchronous KMS calls in hot path, (B) increase auth timeout in gateway to tolerate brief KMS throttles, (C) roll back the new auth change that introduced synchronous KMS calls. Which is fastest?
Miguel (Eng): Quickest is C (rollback to previous auth-proxy config) — I'm prepping the rollback. Also will follow up with A as durable fix.
DeployBot: deploy request queued: auth-proxy v3.3.0 -> v3.2.1 (rollback) on eu-1 (deploy id d-775).
Alex (SRE): Rolling rollback now. I'll watch error rate and traces. Adding temporary alert suppression for noisy downstream alerts during rollback.
Miguel (Eng): Rollback started, expected 5-8m to finish across eu-1 pool.
Priya (CS): I told acme-app we're investigating and asked them to hold off retries for 30s while we test. They asked for ETA and root cause once resolved.
Alex (SRE): Error rate dropped from 8% -> 0.6% ~90s after rollback finished. Confirming in logs that auth-proxy no longer hitting KMS sync path.
Priya (CS): Acme-app confirms errors stopped and performance returned to normal. They've accepted interim update.
Sara (PM): Great. Capture RCA and follow-ups. Proposed action items now: 
  1) Postmortem write-up (owner: Miguel) — include timeline, config diff, and repro. due: 2026-03-16 EOD.
  2) Implement local token cache/circuit-breaker in auth-proxy (owner: Miguel) — add unit + integration tests, staged rollout. due: 2026-03-23.
  3) Add alert: p95 token refresh > 500ms in eu region + dashboard panel for KMS 429 trend (owner: Alex). due: 2026-03-17.
  4) Update incident runbook to include KMS-throttle mitigation steps and customer comms templates (owner: Priya). due: 2026-03-18.
  5) Customer comms: send a short post-incident note to acme-app and other affected customers (owner: Priya). ASAP.
Miguel (Eng): I'll open the PR for token cache today and attach load test results. Also will include a simulated KMS 429 test.
Alex (SRE): I'll add the alert and a quick dashboard. Also proposing a safe default auth timeout bump from 2s -> 5s for eu gateways while we harden the cache.
Priya (CS): Drafted a short message to customers: "We identified an auth proxy change that increased KMS calls in the hot path causing intermittent 5xxs. We've rolled back the change and implemented mitigations. Full postmortem to follow." I'll send after Miguel adds the postmortem link.
Nora (Oncall): Noting follow-up: runbook step to temporarily increase gateway auth timeout and enable local cache toggle during throttles.
DeployBot: deploy auth-proxy v3.2.1 completed on eu-1 (deploy id d-775) in 6m.
Alex (SRE): Closing incident channel for active mitigation; leaving follow-up action items in tracker. If anyone sees resurgence, reopen.
Priya (CS): Thanks everyone — marking this customer escalation resolved for now. :thumbsup:
